start_here: Say to your AI: "I rewrote the voice-over, so move the events in bakery/events.piece.json to where their words now play in bakery/new-words.json." It runs tool:re-time-events-tied-to-words.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON. For this folder the account row holds your own dimensions registry.
alike: a config sheet or settings spreadsheet
a notes page of defaults per project

instructions: 1. Have a piece JSON whose event tokens carry bound_to (the phrase, an edge start or end, an offset in seconds, optionally a slot and which repeat), for example an event bound to "sold them all" at its start with offset -0.1.
2. Get a word-timed transcript of the rewritten voice-over from any speech-to-text tool: {"words":[{"text","start","end"}]}, saved as bakery/new-words.json.

3. Say to your AI: "Re-time my events to the new words". It reads the row with tools:list and runs python3 -I tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/do-work/retime.py bakery/events.piece.json bakery/new-words.json bakery/events.retimed.json --report
4. Read how many events moved and where each went. An event whose words are not in the new transcript keeps its time and is listed as unmatched: decide what it should follow, never accept a guess.
5. Events keep their length when they have an end time (t1).
6. Optional: if you keep your own dimensions registry as a row of list:settings, read that row with records:read, write it to a file and add --settings-record FILE to the command.

worked_examples.title: One event follows its phrase, one is left unmatched
worked_examples.ask: Move my events to where their words now play.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/do-work/retime.py and run for real. bakery/events.piece.json has ev-sold (t 2.0 to 3.5, bound to "sold them all", edge start, offset -0.1) and ev-close (t 5.0, bound to "closing time", edge end). bakery/new-words.json is "Sam baked 52 loaves then sold them all", one word every 0.5 s from 1.0 s: python3 -I tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/do-work/retime.py bakery/events.piece.json bakery/new-words.json bakery/events.retimed.json --report
worked_examples.hands_back: Exit 0 and: bakery/events.retimed.json: 1 of 2 bound tokens re-timed from the new words; ev-sold: moved: 'sold them all' 2.0 -> 3.4; ev-close: unmatched: 'closing time' 5.0 -> 5.0 (these words are not in the new transcript; the time is unchanged).

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for tool settings and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and list:settings as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
